title: Realistic token-stream simulator for multi-tenant SSE/WebSocket workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a high-fidelity load testing harness that simulates token-level streaming chat/completion traffic over SSE and WebSocket. The simulator must model realistic multi-tenant behavior: connection churn, variable token rates per session, KV cache priming and warm/cold prefixes, prompt variety (short/long multi-turn), network jitter, and auth token rotation. Primary metrics: sustained tokens/sec, per-request p95 for first-byte and token-arrival, error-rate, reconnection frequency, and per-tenant throughput. The harness must export structured telemetry compatible with existing Grafana/Prometheus dashboards and emit baseline runs for automatic regression detection.
acceptance_criteria: Generates > 250k tokens/sec aggregate on a 16-GPU Dedicated testbed across 5 simulated tenants with configurable distribution
Captures p95 for first-byte (TTFB) and per-token arrival time per endpoint type (SSE/WebSocket) and stores results in the perf datastore
Supports KV cache priming scenarios (cold, partially-warm, fully-warm) and can assert cache hit ratios during a run
Provides two workload profiles: conversational-churn (many short sessions) and long-completion (few long sessions), including a mixed profile that mirrors production percentiles
Integrates with regression-alerting pipeline: ability to upload a baseline JSON and fail CI if p95 increases >10% or token/sec drops >15% over baseline
steps: Design event model: define session lifecycle, token emission rates, think-time distributions (log-normal), burst parameters (Poisson arrivals)
Implement core generator with pluggable transport layer (SSE client, WebSocket client, optional HTTP chunked for non-streaming) and token-level timers
Add KV cache priming hooks: replay prefix sequences and mark 'warm' sessions to measure hit/miss behavior
Wire telemetry: Prometheus client + JSON run artifact (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, error breakdown, reconnections)
Create dashboard templates and a baseline ingestion tool for the regression pipeline
Run synthetic validation on staging: verify token accounting, reconnection semantics, and stable metrics under noise
Publish README, examples, and a smoke test; create a GitHub PR and request runtime team review
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff — defined workload profiles and metric set. Agreed on two canonical profiles: conversational-churn and long-completion. (Aisha)
2025-02-13: Prototype SSE client implemented using existing client lib; validated token-level timers locally. Observed deterministic per-token pacing across 3k concurrent sessions. (Lukas)

2025-02-14: Integration test revealed inaccurate KV hit accounting when sessions multiplex across GPUs — root cause: session ID hash used for routing omitted tenant namespace. Patch proposed in PR #482. (Lukas)

2025-02-16: Design review with runtime team — discussed backpressure handling and graceful per-connection pause/resume for SSE. Decided to model client-side read window and simulate paused reads to reproduce real-app slow-consumers. (Design feedback: Casey)
2025-02-18: Added regression upload CLI and baseline JSON format. Created initial Grafana dashboard (link below). Preparing PR for review. (Aisha)
tradeoffs: Fidelity vs cost: High-fidelity simulations (per-token timers + rich prompt sets) are expensive; we'll provide lightweight sampled profiles for CI and full-fidelity runs for nightly/regression jobs.
Determinism vs realism: Fully stochastic arrival models are better for production likeness but make test failures noisy. We'll allow deterministic seeds for repeatable baseline comparisons.
In-harness telemetry vs external scraping: Exporting in-run JSON artifacts simplifies regression checks but increases I/O; Prometheus scraping preferred for continuous dashboards.
Multiplexing: Reusing a single process for many simulated sessions reduces infra cost but risks head-of-line scheduling artifacts; recommend scaling horizontally for large token/sec targets.
